source_method: Public iFixit owner follow-ups and YouTube video description chapter markers; no video frames/transcript inspected.
protocol: Two outcome-blinded diagnostic checkpoints per case; keep documented intervention and outcome in oracle, never feed oracle to Circuit-AI.

cases.title: Original Game Boy stops powering on after long storage
cases.device_hint: Nintendo Game Boy DMG-01 original handheld

source.title: Why will my Game Boy not turn on?

full_breakdown.event: Owner says inherited original Game Boy had been in storage for years and once ran after a basic clean; after subsequent storage it no longer powered on.
Other repairers suggest checking correct, functioning batteries, terminals, corrosion and then power-board condition if initial checks do not help.
Owner reports visible corrosion on the battery terminals, gentle cleaning with a small quantity of vinegar, and installation of checked fresh batteries.
Owner reports console boots after terminal cleaning and battery replacement; contribution of each individual action was not isolated.
Owner then notices missing vertical pixel lines in the LCD. The thread only suggests another repair, without an owner-confirmed display fix.

checkpoints.title: Original Nintendo Game Boy no power
checkpoints.device_hint: Nintendo original Game Boy retro handheld DMG-01
symptoms: Original Game Boy will not turn on after long storage
Previously started with batteries but now shows no sign of starting
checkpoints.notes: Battery age, battery-contact state, board and display are not yet inspected. No physical measurements provided.

checkpoints.title: Original Nintendo Game Boy no power after corrosion inspection
checkpoints.device_hint: Nintendo original Game Boy retro handheld DMG-01
symptoms: Original handheld does not boot
Battery terminals have visible corrosion
Known-good batteries are available for a controlled retest
checkpoints.notes: Contact corrosion is an observed clue, not proof of sole root cause; device has not yet been cleaned or retested in this checkpoint.

oracle.source_reported_hardware_intervention: Cleaned corroded battery terminals and used checked new batteries
oracle.source_reported_result: Power restored/boots, but vertical LCD lines absent
oracle.underlying_cause_certainty: battery terminal corrosion is plausible and owner-observed, but effect of new batteries versus cleaning not separately isolated

cases.engineering_lesson: Prevent a boot success from being promoted to a complete-functioning-product success when LCD remains faulty.

cases.title: 12-inch 2015 MacBook fails to start or charge

full_breakdown.event: Owner reports 2015 12-inch MacBook does not start after overnight charging and stays cold; suspects battery or USB-C charging port.
Owner checks the charger and a second known-working charger; neither starts this MacBook, although they power another compatible device.
Owner reports the indicator on one USB-C cable flickers only with this MacBook, unlike steady illumination on an iPad. This is not a direct electrical current measurement.
Repairer notes USB-C charging port is a likely candidate but keeps charger and battery alternatives open; recommends structured checks.
Owner says replacement port and battery have been ordered; the thread does not state unambiguously which parts were ultimately installed.
Owner reports root problem was the USB-C port and MacBook is fixed. No instrument readings or extended load test are provided.

checkpoints.title: Retina MacBook 2015 no boot
symptoms: MacBook does not power on even after charging overnight
Device is cold to touch and gives no startup response
checkpoints.notes: No measured charge current. Charging cable, battery, USB-C port and board paths have not yet been isolated.

checkpoints.title: Retina MacBook 2015 intermittent charging connection
symptoms: MacBook still does not power on
Two chargers work on other devices but not this MacBook
One USB-C cable's indicator flickers when attached to MacBook
checkpoints.notes: No actual measured USB-C power delivery values. Battery and charging-port diagnosis still needs physical confirmation.

oracle.source_reported_hardware_intervention: Owner ordered replacement USB-C port and battery; later states charging port was the culprit, but exact installed parts not documented
oracle.underlying_cause_certainty: charging port identified by owner's follow-up; no board-level meter readings shared

cases.engineering_lesson: Known-good charger and intermittent indicator can prioritize port/connector but do not prove root cause or justify board replacement.

cases.title: iPhone 6s still fails to charge after a port replacement

source.title: Phone not charging after charging port replacement

full_breakdown.event: Original Lightning port charged intermittently only when cable was pushed or angled; owner replaced the charging-port assembly.
After replacement, phone no longer charges. Screen, microphone, speaker and headphone connection reportedly still function; depleted battery causes a brief boot then shutdown when plugged in.
Repair adviser suggests returning to original port as a diagnostic A/B test with battery disconnected first, rather than immediately assuming logic-board chip damage.
Owner reconnects old port and finds charging still possible when the connector is pressed firmly. The original port is still mechanically unreliable.
Adviser infers replacement flex may be defective and suggests a known-good replacement. No owner follow-up proves the final working fix.

checkpoints.title: iPhone 6s charging still fails after assembly replacement
checkpoints.device_hint: Apple iPhone 6s smartphone with Lightning connector
symptoms: Charging was intermittent with original Lightning port
After replacing charge-port flex the phone does not charge at all
Battery depleted; phone momentarily starts on charger then shuts down
Other phone functions were reported working
checkpoints.notes: Replacement flex compatibility/function is unverified. Do not assume motherboard IC fault; old port has not yet been reconnected in this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: iPhone 6s original-port A/B comparison after failed replacement
checkpoints.device_hint: Apple iPhone 6s smartphone with Lightning connector
symptoms: Newly installed Lightning charging flex does not support charging
Reconnecting old original port restores partial charging if plug is held at an angle
Battery ran down after failed replacement
checkpoints.notes: A/B observation raises suspicion of faulty replacement flex or connection; no measured charge current or final verified new replacement. The phone is not yet fully restored.

oracle.source_reported_initial_fault: Intermittent charging became no charging after replacement flex
oracle.source_reported_hardware_intervention: Owner reattached original flex; original port charges only while pressed firmly
oracle.source_reported_result: Original partly works; suggested replacement part failure not independently established; no final owner-confirmed repair
oracle.underlying_cause_certainty: A/B observation supports suspected defective replacement flex or installation, not proven component failure; upstream charging fault remains

cases.engineering_lesson: Detect a bad replacement part and isolate through A/B evidence, not overclaim a logic board fault or successful phone restoration.
